and the opt-in QEMU raspi4b lane (scripts/qemu-rpi4-test.sh). Generated 2026-11-10.

bcm2711-rpi-4-b-qemu-raspi4b.dtb
  The tree QEMU 11.1.3 `raspi4b` passes the kernel for bcm2711-rpi-4-b.dtb:
  QEMU adds /memory and /chosen and replaces the PCIe, RNG200, thermal and
  GENET nodes with FDT_NOP (hw/arm/raspi4b.c, fdt_nop_node).
    qemu-system-aarch64 -M raspi4b,dumpdtb=bcm2711-rpi-4-b-qemu-raspi4b.dtb \
        -dtb bcm2711-rpi-4-b.dtb -kernel <any kernel8.img> -display none
  sha256 e72a5e4e70b0d80379ae66260afbf6c8dece41f48407a702e707626a33bd3451

t8103-j274.dtb
  Linux v7.3 arch/arm64/boot/dts/apple/t8103-j274.dts (Mac mini M1), with its
  includes (t8103.dtsi, t8103-jxxx.dtsi, t8103-pmgr.dtsi, spi1-nvram.dtsi,
  hwmon-*.dtsi, include/dt-bindings/...) fetched from
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v7.3/, compiled with
    cpp -nostdinc -undef -D__DTS__ -x assembler-with-cpp -I include \
        -I arch/arm64/boot/dts/apple arch/arm64/boot/dts/apple/t8103-j274.dts \
      | dtc -I dts -O dtb -q -o t8103-j274.dtb          # DTC 1.7.0 (Ubuntu noble)
  Its cpu-release-addr properties are <0 0>: the loader fills them in.
  sha256 0b14301f40b35d14b12c9571811b2fe9529643a2b0293c60cedadd33a0224147

t8103-j274-m1n1.dtb
  t8103-j274.dtb after an m1n1-style in-place fill of every cpu-release-addr
  (m1n1 points each at its spin-table entry; the addresses here model a
  64-byte-stride table at 0x8_03a0_0000, entry offset 16), in /cpus order:
    i=0; for c in 0 1 2 3 10100 10101 10102 10103; do
      a=$((0x803a00000 + i*64 + 16))
      fdtput -t x t8103-j274-m1n1.dtb /cpus/cpu@$c cpu-release-addr \
          $(printf '0x%x 0x%x' $((a>>32)) $((a & 0xffffffff))); i=$((i+1)); done
  sha256 b616b6478ba040fbbd6c05dc1adb5c508e78595a7ef045646a27ceb622faea0b
